title: Pocket Dial
mood: tender and blurred, holding on to something ordinary
subject: a four-minute pocket-dial voicemail of your father washing up and whistling
caption: Shoegaze revival in the current nu-gaze style. Walls of fuzz guitar through a heavy fuzz pedal, with glide-guitar whammy bends and reverse-reverb swells, drop-tuned so the low chords feel heavy; a bass guitar doubling the root notes underneath; drums washed in constant ride and crash with the snare half-buried; a single quiet clean guitar playing alone in the intro. Loud, blurred and wide, the guitars dominant, the voice sitting just inside the guitars and slightly clearer in the verses. Female voice, breathy and airy in a soft high register, sitting just inside the guitars with every word still audible. 84 BPM, D major. Tender and blurred, holding on to something ordinary. No clean pop vocal on top, no trap drums, no autotune, no metal growls, no acoustic folk strumming, no pedal steel or slowcore.
lyrics:
[Intro - one clean guitar, then a fuzz swell, short]

[Verse 1]
Tuesday, six-fourteen, a missed call from Dad
Four minutes twelve seconds and nobody talking
Just the tap running and the radio on low
And him whistling the same three notes

[Chorus]
Pocket dial, pocket dial
You don't know I'm listening
Plates in the rack and the kettle starting
Pocket dial

[Verse 2]
I can hear the dog's tags on her bowl
I can hear you tell her not yet
You say right then to nobody at all
You've said that every evening I can remember

[Chorus]
Pocket dial, pocket dial
You don't know I'm listening
I won't call back, you'd only say hello
Pocket dial

[Instrumental Break - fuzz guitar wall with glide bends]

[Bridge - guitars swell and blur]
I saved it to the cloud, I saved it twice
Four minutes twelve seconds of you washing up

[Outro - fuzz falls away, clean guitar alone]
I play it on the train when it's dark out
It ends when you sit down on the phone
